title: IQM Researchers Benchmark Projected Quantum Kernels Across 45 Qubits Using Cross-Device Referee-Challenger Protocol - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IQM and QbitSoft benchmarked projected quantum kernels at 15-45 qubits on IQM Emerald and Garnet using a cross-device referee-challenger protocol that prevents QML models from fitting device noise, showing up to a 30-point gap over classical baselines; but a classical MPS simulator reproduced the 45-qubit circuit in under 20 seconds, so no quantum advantage is claimed.

insights.claim: IQM and QbitSoft researchers used a cross-device referee-challenger framework, where one processor assigns labels and an independent processor or separate qubit chain competes against classical models, to prevent quantum machine learning models from inflating accuracy by fitting device-specific hardware noise.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Highlights a credible methodology for judging QML claims; benchmarks lacking such controls may overstate results.

insights.claim: The IQM projected quantum kernel workflow builds on a protocol introduced by Google researchers, encoding Fashion-MNIST image components into a second-order Trotterized 1D Heisenberg Hamiltonian and competing against 11 classical baselines including kernel SVMs, gradient boosting, random forests and neural networks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Engineered classification tasks favor quantum kernels by design; results are not general ML wins.
insights.locator: Building on the engineered classification protocol

insights.claim: In a 15-qubit shallow cross-chip experiment (IQM Emerald referee, IQM Garnet challenger), the quantum model reached 81% accuracy versus 51% for the best classical model, a statistically significant 30-point gap.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shallow circuits on current hardware can show large engineered-task gaps.
insights.locator: IQM Projected Quantum Kernel Hardware & Error-Mitigation Benchmarks

insights.claim: In a deep unmitigated 15-qubit experiment (10 Trotter steps, depth 129, 441 CZ gates), quantum accuracy dropped to 68% versus 64% for the best classical model, a non-significant 4-point gap.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Noise at depth erases quantum edge, underscoring the need for error mitigation and correction.
insights.locator: IQM Projected Quantum Kernel Hardware & Error-Mitigation Benchmarks

insights.claim: At 30 and 45 qubits on disjoint chains of the 54-qubit IQM Emerald, projected quantum kernels maintained a 17- to 28-point gap over 11 classical ML models.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gap persists at scale on engineered tasks.
insights.locator: IQM Projected Quantum Kernel Hardware & Error-Mitigation Benchmarks

insights.claim: For deep 15-qubit projected-kernel circuits, readout error mitigation added 0 points, zero-noise extrapolation restored 14 points via label shifts, and IQM's adaptive Pauli twirling restored 17 points and halved feature noise.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Mitigation technique choice materially changes QML outcomes.
insights.locator: IQM Projected Quantum Kernel Hardware & Error-Mitigation Benchmarks

insights.claim: Zero-noise extrapolation widened the measured classification gap by altering the referee's labeling bandwidth rather than fixing features, whereas IQM's adaptive Pauli twirling reduced feature residuals directly, bringing IQM Emerald's accuracy on ideal labels to within 2.5 percentage points of a noise-free processor.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Some error-mitigation gains can be artefacts; investors should scrutinize how mitigation produces reported advantages.
insights.locator: Comparing mitigated hardware runs against noiseless

insights.claim: A classical matrix product state simulator with bond dimension 128 reproduced IQM's 45-qubit projected-kernel circuit in under 20 seconds, matching the QPU (72% vs. 73%), so future experiments targeting genuine quantum advantage will move to harder-to-simulate 2D quantum dynamics.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: The results are classically simulable; genuine QML advantage claims remain unproven.
insights.locator: Comparing mitigated hardware runs against noiseless
